question: In spring and summer, steady winds blow south along California's coast. What do they do to the coastal sea?
options: Warm it, piling surface water ashore
Cool it, drawing deep water up
answer: Cool it, drawing deep water up. On a spinning planet, water pushed by the wind moves on average at right angles to it: to the right in the northern hemisphere, here out to sea. Cold, nutrient-rich water rises to replace it, feeding the coast's fisheries and chilling the air into San Francisco's summer fog.
move: A push does not always move things the way it points.
trap: Barely change it, as if the water simply moved with the wind.
source: Talley et al., Descriptive Physical Oceanography, 2011
reference: Talley, Pickard, Emery & Swift, Descriptive Physical Oceanography: An Introduction, 6th edition, Academic Press, 2011
